 About the festival
 PintorRock 2026 takes place in Reus from Thursday 29 to Saturday 31 October , with 30 punk, street rock, ska and hardcore bands spread across three days. It is the 15th anniversary edition of a festival founded in 2011 and the second at Parc de la Festa , at Camí del Roquís, 31-37. The line-up and the day-by-day stage times have now been published, and the only official ticket outlet is Enterticket .
 PintorRock 2026 line-up and stage times by day
 All three days finish at 03:30 and no sets overlap. The concerts take place under a large covered marquee. Thursday is the shortest day and the only one that opens in the afternoon; on Friday and Saturday the music starts at midday.
 Thursday 29 (doors at 16:00 ) leans on the international names: Kuerpospin (16:30), Baya Baye (17:30), Italian band Bull Brigade (18:50), Kaos Urbano (20:10), Envidia Kotxina (21:40), The Toy Dolls at 23:10 , the hip hop punk of Moscow Death Brigade (00:50) and Bihotza (02:20).
 Friday 30 (doors at 11:30 ) is the longest day and the one with the most street rock. Kamikazes (12:00), Rat-Zinger (13:10), Biznaga (14:30), Periferia (15:50), Josetxu Piperrak (17:10) and Inadaptats (18:30) open proceedings, and the big stretch comes with Boikot at 20:05 , El Drogas at 21:50 and Narco at 23:35 . The early hours belong to La Élite (01:10) and Amygdala (02:20).
 Saturday 31 (doors at 11:30 ) kicks off with The Lizards (12:00), Bala (13:00), Benito Kamelas (14:20), Manifa (15:40), El Último ke zierre (17:00) and Los de Marras (18:20). Then come Soziedad Alkoholika at 20:00 , Segismundo Toxicómano at 21:40 and The Baboon Show at 23:20 , with Crim (01:00) and Me fritos & the gimme cheetos (02:30) closing.
 Anyone going mainly for the headliners can arrive in the late afternoon without missing the main acts: each day's biggest block starts from 20:00. Between sets, songs by the 159 bands that entered the festival's first competition will be played. The full breakdown, in detail, is in our news story on the PintorRock 2026 stage times .
 Tickets and prices: €78 pass, in the final price tier
 The three-day pass costs €78 from midnight on 22 October: the €76 tier has sold out and the festival described that increase as the last price change. Day tickets remain at €35 for Thursday , €45 for Friday and €50 for Saturday . On that same 22 October, the organisers put capacity at 97% , and on the 25th they warned on Instagram that the last tickets remained, so there is little time left to decide. Children under 10 get in free with an authorisation form and the festival accepts the Bono Cultural Joven . Tickets are not in the holder's name, but it is advisable to bring a DNI, passport or driving licence as you may be asked for it at the entrance; if you share a photo of your ticket, cover the QR code.
 If they do not sell out, passes and day tickets will remain available online and at the box office, even during the festival. Tickets are exchanged for an electronic wristband at the box office, which opens on Thursday from 11:00 to 03:00 and on Friday and Saturday from 10:00 to 03:00 . Each person must collect their own.
 Inside the site, you pay with that wristband, which works as a cashless system. Advance top-ups from home are open until Wednesday 28 October at 23:59 : €60 with €5 free or €120 with €15 free. Any remaining balance can be claimed back from 10 to 17 November, except the free credit.
 Camping, camper area and getting there without an official bus
 Camping costs €15 per person for the three nights, is not sold by the day and is not included in concert tickets. It has 2,500 places, a minute from the site, and 7,500 square metres more than in 2025 for the same capacity. It opens on the morning of Thursday 29, although sources disagree on the time: the FAQs on the website say 10:00 and the Enterticket ticket says 11:00 , after collecting your wristband at the box office. You can camp until 12:00 on Sunday 1 November. Space is allocated on a first-come, first-served basis and no stoves of any kind are allowed.
 The camper area is free , requires no booking, is 300 metres from the concerts and open from Wednesday 28. It accepts vans, motorhomes, caravans and trailer tents, but not tents next to the vehicle. Next to the campsite is the communal area, with a 24-hour bar, breakfasts, phone charging and a shower truck where each shower costs €3.
 An important change for people coming from elsewhere: there will be no official bus this year . The festival had announced services from Barcelona, Lleida and Girona, but the organisers have cancelled them, so you will have to make your own way to Reus. Without a car, the most direct option is the train: Reus station has regional services to Barcelona on Rodalies lines R14 and R15 , and from there it is about 1.7 kilometres on foot to Parc de la Festa, just over 20 minutes. The concerts end at 03:30 and there is no shuttle, so it is worth planning your return before you go.
 What you can bring in and how to pay inside
 The wristband is the only means of payment at bars, food trucks and official merchandise stands; only the bands' stalls take payment separately. Any balance not claimed between 10 and 17 November will go to the strike fund of the Sindicat de Llogateres.
 You can bring food, but not drink , into the concert area; free water is available at the bars. The ground is sand, there is a ramp for people with reduced mobility, lockers can be booked to leave your backpack and animals are not allowed. You can leave and re-enter by scanning your wristband at the reader at each entrance.
 Minors can attend with the authorisation form for their age: 10 to 15-year-olds accompanied by an authorised adult, and 16 and 17-year-olds without an adult but with the authorisation form and a photocopy of the DNI of their mother, father or guardian. The forms and the rest of the rules are in the PintorRock FAQs .
